Customer Admin (ACME Corp): Hey team — after our IdP metadata refresh earlier today, users can't SSO into Redwood. Getting a generic "SAML login failed" in the UI for multiple users. No config changes on our side aside from the metadata URL swap. Any quick checks?

Alex (Support): Sorry about that — can you confirm the metadata URL you pushed and whether you see any 4xx/5xx when we fetch it? Also, Slack-style: are you seeing errors in our side or only client-side?

Customer Admin (ACME Corp): URL is https://idp.acme.com/saml/metadata (redirects to https://idp.acme.com/.well-known/saml/meta.xml). No 4xx when I curl it.

SAML-bot: IdP metadata for acme.com was updated at 1901234000 (automated pull). Detected 2 KeyDescriptor elements without explicit use attribute.

Maria (SRE): I pulled our assertion logs. We see repeated failures: "Signature validation failed: no matching signing KeyDescriptor" followed by "No matching ACS found for recipient" for some requests. Pasted examples below:

```
ERROR 2026-03-15T14:42:11Z saml: Signature validation failed: KeyInfo did not match any configured signing cert
WARN 2026-03-15T14:42:12Z saml: Assertion recipient mismatch: expected https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs but got https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/ (trailing slash)
```

Alex (Support): Two separate issues hinted: KeyDescriptor order/use and ACS trailing slash mismatch. Which IdP did you update metadata for? Okta? ADFS?

Customer Admin (ACME Corp): It's an internal IdP (Shibboleth). They said the metadata endpoint was replaced; didn't touch ACS values.

Jordan (Product): Quick repro checklist for SAML problems we use: 1) fetch metadata ourselves 2) check for multiple KeyDescriptor elements + certificate expiration 3) check KeyDescriptor @use attributes and ordering 4) confirm ACS exact match (no extra slash) 5) verify signature algorithm (sha256 vs sha1).

Maria (SRE): I fetched the metadata — looks like Shibboleth emitted two KeyDescriptor blocks, one for signing and one for encryption, but neither have use="signing" explicitly. Order: encryption first, signing second. Our parser prefers explicit use or the first KeyDescriptor if none is marked. When the signing cert is second, our code attempted to validate with the first (encryption) cert and failed.

```
<md:KeyDescriptor>
  <ds:KeyInfo>
    <ds:X509Data><ds:X509Certificate>MIIF...ENCRYPTION_CERT...</ds:X509Certificate></ds:X509Data>
  </ds:KeyInfo>
</md:KeyDescriptor>
<md:KeyDescriptor>
  <ds:KeyInfo>
    <ds:X509Data><ds:X509Certificate>MIIF...SIGNING_CERT...</ds:X509Certificate></ds:X509Data>
  </ds:KeyInfo>
</md:KeyDescriptor>
```

Alex (Support): That matches SAML-bot note. Two ways to fix: ask IdP to add use="signing" to the signing KeyDescriptor or reorder so signing appears first. We can also accept both certs temporarily by configuring an alternate cert in our SSO config, but that requires owner approval.

Customer Admin (ACME Corp): Can you accept both certs on your side? Our IdP team is slower today.

Sam (Oncall): We can add the second cert as an allowed signing cert for this tenant for a short window. Need customer confirmation and a support ticket approval. Also watch for ACS mismatch logs — we should normalise trailing slashes on our ACS matching heuristics as a separate product fix.

Alex (Support): @Customer Admin (ACME Corp) please confirm you want us to add the signing cert from the metadata as an allowed signing cert for your org. If yes, paste the cert block or confirm we should pull it from the metadata URL.

Customer Admin (ACME Corp): Confirm — pull from metadata URL. Also we found the trailing-slash mismatch in our app links; will remove the trailing slash on our side.

Maria (SRE): Done — I pulled the second certificate, added it to the tenant accepted signing certs at 1901234321. I also applied a short-term ACS match tolerance so both https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs and https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/ will be accepted for this tenant. Monitoring auth logs now.

(2m later)

SAML-bot: Initial test assertion validated successfully at 1901234440.

Customer Admin (ACME Corp): Login works now for a test user, thanks! Can you document long-term fix?

Jordan (Product): Action items: 1) Recommend IdP add explicit use="signing" on KeyDescriptor (customer has been advised) 2) Product ticket to make our metadata parser accept explicit use and fallback more deterministically (handle encryption vs signing) — assigning to infra team 3) Product ticket to normalise ACS matching (trailing slash tolerance) 4) Run a scan for tenants with metadata having multiple KeyDescriptor elements and flag ones where signing cert is not first.

Alex (Support): I'll keep this thread open until you confirm full rollout fixed. Closing note: if you rotate certs in future, please notify support or upload metadata with both keys and use attributes to avoid a transient outage. :thumbsup:

Customer Admin (ACME Corp): Will do — appreciate the fast help.

Sam (Oncall): Follow-up: we shouldn't silently accept encryption certs for signing. Temporary acceptance is fine but we need an audit log entry — I added an internal ticket to log this change and an expiry at 1901238000.

Maria (SRE): Logging and expiry set. Marking this as resolved from infra side unless customer re-opens.

Customer Admin (ACME Corp): Confirmed resolved for us. Thanks again! :rocket:
